review.What it does: An AI assistant you install on your computer (Mac, Windows, Linux, phone app coming) that does real work: writes and fixes code, runs commands, browses the web. Ask for an app and it builds it, hosts it at a live link on their cloud, and can pay for the online services it needs from its own crypto wallet.
review.Unique?: Partly. Each piece exists elsewhere: coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), prompt-to-live-app builders (Replit, Lovable, Bolt), local AI (Ollama). The rare part is all of them in one fast app plus a built-in wallet that pays per use (x402). Open source (MIT), so anyone can copy it: the edge is speed of shipping, not secret tech.
review.Scalable?: The software is lean (Rust, starts in 8 ms, 9.5 MB memory). The business is harder: a 2-person team, their own cloud servers cost money per user, and they compete with very well-funded companies. Fine as a niche product; big scale is unproven.
review.Narrative fit: Strong: AI agents, agents that pay for things (x402), open-source local AI. Weak link to Robinhood Chain: the agent's wallet runs on Base, Ethereum, Solana and other EVM chains; Robinhood Chain is only where the token lives.
review.How it makes money: Pro plan $20/month, Team $18 a seat/month, a margin on AI models it resells (priced below the makers' own list prices), and cloud hosting billed by the hour. Token: half of the model margin is meant to buy LETRO back, and paying for credit in LETRO burns 10%.
review.Token today: LETRO does nothing yet: their docs say buying credit with it and staking 'switch on when LETRO launches', and the roadmap still lists buybacks as 'next'. Staking promises 20% a year paid as AI credit (up to $5/day), a real cost the business must cover.
review.Watch for: 1) Buybacks starting, listed with transactions on /tokenomics. 2) X followers growing (169 now vs 4,000+ for the big winners). 3) The team's earlier token $AILE peaked in a month and lost 83%. 4) Cheap model prices may rely on shared subscriptions (their AILE market), which the AI companies' terms generally don't allow.
